# Beautiful UI upstream provenance

These components are copied from the Beautiful UI repository:

- Source: https://github.com/slev12397/beautiful-ui
- Pinned commit: `ff0f74d62d8be9d89bcb735b3632e31a6ccf88dc`
- Reference site: https://www.beautifului.dev/
- License: [BEAUTIFULUI-MIT-LICENSE.txt](./BEAUTIFULUI-MIT-LICENSE.txt)

Copied source files:

- `components/atoms/Button.tsx`
- `components/atoms/Shimmer.tsx`
- `components/atoms/EntityChip.tsx`
- `components/atoms/ValuePill.tsx`
- `components/primitives/GlideMenu.tsx`
- `components/primitives/SidebarNav.tsx`
- `components/primitives/TaskRows.tsx`
- `components/primitives/FilterTable.tsx`
- `components/primitives/LoadingState.tsx`
- `components/primitives/InsightCards.tsx`
- `components/primitives/ContextCards.tsx`
- `lib/utils.ts`
- `app/globals.css` as `styles/beautifului.css`

The DOM structure, Tailwind classes, keyframes, transitions, stagger delays, pixel loader, gliding menu, expandable rows, and filter collapse animation remain from the pinned upstream source. Adaptations are limited to the integration seams:

- `SidebarNav` accepts the product lockup (`brand`: a mark and a name), navigation, recent-history and primary-action data/callbacks and help text; its paid icon imports and demo defaults are replaced with `lucide-react` aliases and Rewindle defaults. Navigation exposes accessible names/current-page state (the selected recent run is marked `aria-current` too), and Settings remains available when collapsed. The upstream workspace switcher (its menu, portal and outside-click handling) is not carried: the app has one product and no workspaces to switch between, so the header is a static lockup, the Rewindle mark (`rewindle-icon.svg`, drawn as given because it carries its own tile) and the name in the primary ink at a semibold weight. Folded, only the mark stays on the rail, and the expand button lies over it: its arrow takes the mark's place while it is pointed at or focused. The decorative chevron before the recent-history heading is not carried either, because it opened nothing. The search field carries a `sidebar-search` class so `styles/app.css` can draw its focus ring on the field: the bare input inside it sits in a box that clips overflow, which cut its own outline off. The collapse and expand buttons are `inert` whenever they do not apply (not `aria-hidden` with a tab index, which left focus on a button that had just faded out), hand focus to each other when the sidebar changes width, and share `aria-expanded`; the expand button is the same 32px as the collapse button and stays centered on the rail glyphs. The page buttons sit in a `nav` landmark named Primary (the `aside` is named Sidebar), and a nav item's optional `shortcut` ("Control+1") becomes its `aria-keyshortcuts` and a note in its tooltip, as does `footerShortcut` for the footer button. The sidebar folds to its icon rail by itself at 700 CSS pixels and narrower (a high zoom does that to a wide window, and the expanded sidebar alone is 224 pixels), can be opened by hand while narrow, and returns to the person's own collapsed or expanded choice when the width goes back up. That choice is kept between launches in `localStorage` under the `storageKey` the app passes (every read and write is in a `try`, and a profile that blocks storage just leaves the width to decide), and until the person has made one a window of 1040 CSS pixels or narrower starts with the sidebar folded. The row of the page you are on is marked by an accent bar on its left edge (`.sidebar-row[aria-current]` and `.sidebar-footer[aria-current]` in `styles/app.css`, the same bar the selected history row has), over the accent tint, with an accent icon. The upstream marked it only with the hover layer's color, which also left the row whenever the pointer was anywhere in the nav (the row no longer carries `group-hover/glide:bg-transparent`). Under forced colors the Highlight fill is the mark, and the bar is left out.
- `Button`'s `secondary` variant hovers to `hover:bg-hover-2` instead of `hover:bg-inset`, because `--inset` is only 1.06:1 from the surface in both themes, so the upstream hover could not be seen. It has two icon-only sizes, `icon` (32px) and `icon-sm` (28px), both the same rounded square, in place of the four different shapes that the close, refresh, theme and dismiss buttons had; `xs` is 26px and `sm` 28px, so a smaller size is never the taller one (they were 28px and 27px). `accent` and `success` take the page's dark ink in the dark theme (white on the dark theme's light teal was 1.7:1), and `success` is the text-grade green (white on the fill green was 3.6:1). The unused `ghost` variant and the `dark:` classes that only repeated `primary`'s own colors are gone.
- `TaskRows` accepts real `pending`, `failed`, and `cancelled` statuses, a neutral numbered `guide` mode, and a neutral `lastRun` status (a check badge and a "Last run" pill for steps the latest run finished while the overall status no longer vouches for them); a `cancelled` step draws the neutral badge, not the failure red, because a stop the user asked for is not a failure; only the upstream `sequence` status uses its timer. Collapsed details are inert and hidden from assistive technology. Status pill text uses the text-grade `--green-ink`, `--red-ink`, and `--orange-ink` tokens. `rows` is required: the upstream's three sample rows (an ice-cream shop's vendor records and supplier emails) are not carried, so none of that wording can reach the page or its bundle.
- `FilterTable` accepts row IDs, mapped and per-row result labels, computed counts, selected rows, row callbacks, controlled filters, an empty state, sort controls, and a class name. `rows` and `labels` are required: the upstream's sample rows and column names are not carried. Collapsed rows are inert and hidden from assistive technology. With a row callback the table is an ARIA grid with row focus: one roving Tab stop, Up/Down/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown move between visible rows, selection is exposed as `aria-selected`, Enter opens details and Space selects. Focus rings on rows are drawn inside the row because the collapse wrapper clips anything outside it, and the chip strip pads for the same reason. The header row is sticky inside the scroller (with matching scroll padding), a trailing per-row button named through `labels.openRow` opens a row for pointer users beside double-click and Enter (it is not a Tab stop; the row is), a visually hidden hint on how to use the rows describes the grid, status pills carry a `lucide-react` icon as well as a color and truncate instead of overflowing, the chip dots use the same tokens as the pills, and the default export is memoized so a parent that passes stable props skips the re-render on every host update.
- `ValuePill` uses the text-grade `--green-ink`, `--orange-ink`, and `--red-ink` tokens for colored text so status text meets WCAG AA on its tint.
- `styles/beautifului.css` defines those text-grade tokens (and their Tailwind colors) next to the semantic fill colors. Its global `:focus-visible` rule no longer sets `border-radius`: the rule is unlayered, so it overrode every `rounded-*` utility and turned a keyboard-focused pill button into a 4px rectangle. The ring now follows each element's own radius. For the same reason `styles/app.css` no longer carries its own `button, input, select { font: inherit }`: Tailwind's preflight already applies that reset in `@layer base`, and as an unlayered rule it overrode the font-size, weight, and line-height utilities of every button, so `Button`, the filter chips, and the sidebar's footer buttons now render at the sizes and weights their classes declare (a 32px `md` button, 13px/500 `sm`, 12px `xs`). Its `body` also no longer paints the demo's diagonal stripe pattern: the app's shell fills the window with `--page`, so the stripes showed only in the blank frame before the interface mounted, in whichever theme the page guessed. The light ramp (`--inset`, `--hover`, `--hover-2`, the lines and `--field`) is defined in `styles/app.css`, warm like the page, rather than taken from the upstream's cool blue-greys. It also carries the app's type scale (`--type-xs` 11px to `--type-3xl` 28px, prefixed so it cannot collide with Tailwind's own `--text-*`, which `Button` uses) and radius scale (`--r-chip` 6, `--r-control` 8, `--r-card` 12, `--r-panel` 18, `--r-pill`); the Tailwind `--radius-*` theme values point at the radius scale, so `rounded-card` and `var(--r-card)` are the same corner. The app's own stylesheets use the scales, nothing the app shows is below 11px (and the host lets the page be zoomed, from 80% to 200% with Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0, or Ctrl and the mouse wheel), and the half-pixel text sizes in the components the app renders are rounded to whole ones. What the app never draws is not carried: the records grid (`.records-*`, about 840 lines), the streaming text and its caret, the context cards' favicon avatars, the animated underline, the component nav scroller, the `primitive-*` spacing utilities and the demo-only keyframes and reveal helpers, and the insight chart tooltip. Only the status-pill colors, the sidebar rules, the shared keyframes the components still name inline (`fade-in`, `fade-up`, `pop-in`, `spin`, `shimmer-text`, `pixel-on`) and `.theme-switching` (which the page uses while a theme swaps) remain of the upstream's component blocks.
- `ContextCards` accepts stable chunk IDs and trailing actions. It and `EntityChip` are not imported anywhere in the app, so the bundler leaves them out; they stay in the tree as upstream source, and `ContextCards` no longer needs a stylesheet class of its own (its header's padding is utilities).
- `InsightCards` accepts an action callback and disabled state, and keeps the upstream page change motion with a keyed `fade-up`. `pages` and `labels` are required: the upstream's three sample pages (the comparison, anomaly and allocation cards, their ice-cream copy and chart data, the `liveline` charts they drew, and the `.insight-chart-*` rules) are not carried, because the app's pages draw their own charts. `liveline` therefore has no importer left; it is still listed in `package.json` and in the bundler's `charts` chunk, which this change did not touch.
- `LoadingState` exports its existing prop shape as an interface for integration, hides the rapidly updating decorative timer from assistive technology, has a `live` prop (on by default) that turns its `status` role off where the page announces the same progress itself, has a `showElapsed` prop (on by default) that turns off its own running clock, and the interval that drives it, where the page already shows an elapsed time from the real source (the loader counts from when it mounted, so beside a run that began earlier it shows a different time). Its `label` is required, and the upstream's `Surfer` variant (a meme video, with its `videoSrc` and the stock labels "Churning" and "Subway surfing") is not carried. The app uses its original pixel and orbit loaders.
